confidence_notes: Food and coffee anchors rest on Numbeo-based aggregates (Expatica, Expat Arrivals, MyLifeElsewhere), converted from GBP to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.33 USD per GBP. Those aggregates gave a draught beer of about £5.3, a cappuccino of about £3.5, an inexpensive meal of about £15 and a mid-range meal for two of about £65. The searches found no Cardiff cocktail or restaurant wine-by-the-glass prices. I set the cocktail and wine anchors from the beer price using typical UK pub and bar ratios, so they are less certain. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates, not checked against any booking pages or listings. They carry the most uncertainty, especially in July, which is peak season and on event or concert nights. The FX figure is the latest RBA rate I found, 0.6720 USD per AUD for 2026-11-18, which was published after the July 2026 pricing window.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with other mid-sized UK regional cities such as Bristol and Manchester. Cardiff's restaurant prices are somewhat below London's, and its accommodation is cheaper than London's but rises in peak season.
